pr_title: Set ambient_intensity to 0.0 in volumetric_fog example, correct doc comment
pr_body:
# Objective

- Fixes #13521

## Solution

Set `ambient_intensity` to 0.0 in volumetric_fog example.

I chose setting it explicitly over changing the default in order to make it clear that this needs to be set depending on whether you have an `EnvironmentMapLight`. See documentation for `ambient_intensity` and related members.

## Testing

- Run the volumetric_fog example and notice how the light shown in #13521 is not there anymore, as expected.
pr_comments:
Linked to [`EnvironmentMapLight`] and went ahead and fixed the preceding links to it as well. It does feel a bit verbose with the `crate::environment_map::` but I guess that's normal(?)

Edit: I formatted the links, should be good now

issue_context.title: Adding VolumetricLight makes objects near the camera brighter
issue_context.body:
## Bevy version

Latest main

## Relevant system information

Windows 10

```
AdapterInfo { name: "AMD Radeon RX 7900 XT", vendor: 4098, device: 29772, device_type: DiscreteGpu, driver: "AMD proprietary driver", driver_info: "24.5.1 (LLPC)", backend: Vulkan }
```

## What you did

Run volumetric_fog example.

## What went wrong

It looks like there is a light at the camera position. By rotating the directional light away completely it becomes obvious:
![image](https://github.com/bevyengine/bevy/assets/23659539/0fc1f57b-372f-410e-83d1-1156271c663a)
See this post to see what it looks like in a "real" scene: https://discord.com/channels/691052431525675048/743663924229963868/1244306327552004116

## Additional information

Removing things like the skybox, bloom, hdr, etc. don't seem to make a difference.
